headline: Building HabitHero taught you how data flows in a real app: from storage, into state, onto the screen — and back again when you tap.

concepts.explanation: Your app is a tree of components. App.js composes screens, screens compose cards, and each component is just a function that returns JSX. HabitCard knows how to draw one habit — nothing more.
concepts.whyItMatters: Small components are easier to read, reuse and fix — every production React Native codebase is organised this way.

quiz.question: Why does the save effect start with `if (isLoading) return;`?
options: Because AsyncStorage can't be used while fonts are loading
To make the app start faster
To avoid overwriting saved habits with the empty starting list
Because useEffect never runs on the first render
quiz.explanation: On the first render `habits` is still `[]`. Without the check, the effect would save that empty list before the load finished — wiping the user's real data.

quiz.question: What could go wrong if toggleHabit did `habit.completedDates.push(today)` and returned the same array?
options: React may not re-render, because the array reference didn't change
The app would crash with a syntax error
AsyncStorage would reject the data
The habit would be deleted
quiz.explanation: React decides whether to re-render by comparing references. Mutating the existing array keeps the same reference, so the UI can silently stay out of date.

quiz.question: Why does TodayScreen use FlatList rather than `habits.map()` inside a ScrollView?
options: ScrollView can't display Text components
FlatList only renders the rows on screen, so long lists stay fast
map() is not supported in React Native
FlatList automatically saves the list to storage
quiz.explanation: A ScrollView renders every child up front. FlatList virtualises the list, drawing only what's visible, which matters as data grows.

quiz.question: What makes the habit name TextInput a *controlled* input?
options: It has a maxLength of 40
It uses returnKeyType="done"
It sits inside a KeyboardAvoidingView
Its value comes from state and onChangeText updates that state
quiz.explanation: Controlled means React state is the single source of truth: `value={name}` displays state and `onChangeText` updates it on every keystroke.

quiz.question: calculateStreak starts counting from yesterday when today isn't checked yet. Why?
options: Because today's date key can't be calculated
To make streaks look bigger than they are
So an unfinished day doesn't break the streak before the day is over
Because a Set can't contain today's key
quiz.explanation: At 9 am you haven't had a chance to do today's habit yet. Counting from yesterday keeps the streak alive until the day actually ends.

challenges.description: Let users change a habit's name, emoji or colour. Long-press should offer Edit and Delete, and editing should reuse the Add Habit form, pre-filled.

hints: Add an optional `timesPerWeek` field to the Habit model and a picker in the form.
